svg.title: Windows 365 or Azure Virtual Desktop: who manages what
svg.desc: Users connect through the Azure Virtual Desktop connection services (gateway, broker and web client), which both Windows 365 and Azure Virtual Desktop use. Windows 365 is software as a service with a fixed fee per licensed user: Microsoft manages the Cloud PC, its network and the Azure resources, and you manage Microsoft Entra ID, DNS, Windows, apps, security and Intune policies. Azure Virtual Desktop is platform as a service with consumption-based pricing: Microsoft runs the service and you manage session host VMs, images, the virtual network, storage and host pools.
svg.text: Both use the Azure Virtual Desktop connection services
Gateway, broker and web client services, run by Microsoft
Shown with the recommended setup (note below)
You build it in your own Azure subscription
Cloud PCs and the Cloud PC infrastructure
Its own Azure subscription and resource groups
Windows and your apps on the Cloud PC
Instead of the Microsoft-hosted network, you manage:
Your Azure subscription and resource groups
The virtual network, routing, VPN or ExpressRoute
The AVD service and its supporting
infrastructure, such as the gateway and broker
Session host virtual machines and their disks
Images (your own, or from the Azure Gallery)
Identity: Microsoft Entra join or hybrid join
Host pools, desktops and apps you publish
Capacity and cost, for example autoscale
The Azure resources and their costs
Fixed monthly fee per licensed user
Flex licenses are pooled for the tenant
Internal users also need an eligible license
Windows 365 lists show the recommended setup: a Microsoft-hosted network, Microsoft Entra join
and gallery images with Windows Autopatch.
